newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria hopes mark peg may lure German investors.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria hopes mark peg may lure German investors.

text.p: Bulgaria's prime minister designate Ivan Kostov said on Thursday pegging the lev to the mark in a fixed exchange rate regime could attract more German investors.

Kostov, leader of the Union of Democratic Forces, said he had discussed with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl the introduction of a currency board mechanism to restore confidence in the national currency.

"We discussed...the proposal made by the caretaker government, which I personally accept, to peg the Bulgarian lev to the German mark and this was met with interest," Kostov told reporters on arrival from a two-day visit to Germany.
"The Chancellor said this could be the greatest encouragement to German investors and this is obviously so."
Kostov said he and interim prime minister Stefan Sofianski had met potential investors and had presented the government's programme.
Kostov left for Germany a few hours after he was formally asked by President Petar Stoyanov on Wednesday to form a government following his party's victory in April 19 elections.
Germany is Bulgaria's biggest trade partner and investor. Sofianski said 40 percent of foreign investments in Bulgaria came from Germany.

Under the currency board system the lev will be pegged to an anchor currency, at a rate that cannot be adjusted. The amount of levs in circulation must be matched precisely by the amount of foreign exchange reserves.
An International Monetary Fund mission is currently in Sofia to discuss final preparations for its introduction.

Traditionally the dollar has been perceived as benchmark of stability as Bulgarians convert their savings mostly into dollars. The bulk of Bulgaria's $9.6 billion foreign debt is also denominated in dollars.
But the dollar is relatively strong at the moment, and a peg to the U.S. currency could make the lev uncompetitive compared to its trading partners within a few months. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-91188
